the denitrification rate of constructed wetlands was closely related to the root exude amount of different macrophyte species.
the root exudates of macrophytes could be used as a carbon source for the denitrification process.

the role of root exudates derived from macrophyte species in constructed wetlands, and provides a new insight into the mechanism of denitrification in the wetlands.
the role of root exudate in microbial denitrifying process in CWs.
the effect of carbon source derived by macrophytes on the microbial denitrification process.

root exudation from macrophytes is the key factor for microbial denitrification.
root exudates of macrophytes can be a carbon source for denitrification and the contribution is related to the plant species.

the root exudates derived from macrophyte species can serve as a carbon source to promote the NO3− transformation in constructed wetlands, which may provide a theoretical basis for the selection of macrophytes in constructed wetlands.
